summary: Build an automated used car price comparison system that crawls auto dealer websites (Autotrader, Cars.com, etc.) to gather and track used car prices over time. The system uses Python for scraping, Scrapy/Selenium for crawling, and MongoDB for data storage, with the goal of comparing prices for specific car models over time.
architectural_notes: Python-based scraping stack: Scrapy for structured crawling, Selenium for JavaScript-heavy pages
MongoDB as primary data store for flexible schema car listing documents
Target sources: Autotrader, Cars.com, and other major auto dealer websites
Internet Identity integration for authentication, enabling per-user data isolation for watchlists and saved searches
known_issues: Anti-scraping measures (CAPTCHAs, IP blocking, rate limiting) on target sites like Autotrader and Cars.com will require proxy rotation and CAPTCHA-solving strategies

Build a price statistics summary panel for a selected car model showing: lowest recorded price, highest recorded price, average price, number of listings, and which source has the cheapest average. Display this alongside or above the price comparison chart.

new_feature_requests.summary: Web scraper using Scrapy/Selenium to crawl Autotrader, Cars.com and other auto dealer sites for used car listings
MongoDB data storage layer to persist scraped car listing data including price, model, year, mileage, dealer info
Price comparison feature to track and compare prices for specific car models over time
Automated scheduling system to periodically re-crawl sources and update price data

Create a backend data model and actor to store used car listings with fields: make, model, year, mileage, price, trim, condition, dealer name, source (e.g., 'Autotrader', 'Cars.com', 'Manual'), listing URL, and timestamp. Support create, read, update, and delete operations for listings.

Create a backend function to retrieve price history for a specific car model (filtered by make + model + optionally year/trim), returning a time-sorted list of price snapshots suitable for charting trends over time.
CSV bulk import feature: allow users to paste or upload a CSV of car listings to quickly load batches of data without manual entry one-by-one

Add a backend function that accepts an array of listing records (same fields as the existing ListingData: make, model, year, mileage, price, trim, condition, dealer name, source, listing URL, timestamp) and bulk-inserts them into the Map store, returning the count of successfully imported records.
Deal score/rating feature: automatically flag listings as 'Good Deal,' 'Fair,' or 'Overpriced' based on how the listing price compares to the average price for that make/model

Add a backend query function `getDealScores` that, for a given make and model, computes the average price across all matching listings and returns each listing ID annotated with a deal score: 'Good Deal' if the listing price is more than 10% below average, 'Overpriced' if more than 10% above average, and 'Fair' otherwise.
Export to CSV: allow users to download comparison reports as CSV files from the dashboard or comparison view
Add filtering options to the CSV export functionality so users can export only specific subsets of listings (e.g., filter by make, model, year range, price range, source, deal score before exporting)
Add saved filter presets feature so users can save, name, and quickly re-apply their favorite filter configurations on the dashboard and comparison export panels

Add a saved filter presets system to the backend that stores named filter configurations. Implement backend functions: `saveFilterPreset(name: Text, filterJson: Text, presetType: Text) : async Nat` (returns preset ID), `getFilterPresets(presetType: Text) : async [FilterPreset]` (where FilterPreset includes id, name, filterJson, presetType, createdAt), `deleteFilterPreset(id: Nat) : async Bool`, and `renameFilterPreset(id: Nat, newName: Text) : async Bool`. Store presets in a stable in-memory map alongside existing listing data.
Add multi-user support with Internet Identity login so each user can save their own watchlists and searches independently

Update the backend actor to scope all per-user data (filter presets, and any future watchlist/search entries) by the caller's Internet Identity principal. Modify `saveFilterPreset`, `getFilterPresets`, `deleteFilterPreset`, and `renameFilterPreset` so that each preset is stored and retrieved relative to the authenticated caller's principal (using `msg.caller`). A user must only see and mutate their own presets. Unauthenticated callers (anonymous principal) should receive an empty list or an error as appropriate.

Add a `Watchlist` data structure to the backend. Implement: `addToWatchlist(make: Text, model: Text, label: ?Text) : async Nat` (returns watchlist entry ID), `getWatchlist() : async [WatchlistEntry]` (returns all watchlist entries for the calling principal), `removeFromWatchlist(id: Nat) : async Bool`. Each `WatchlistEntry` includes id, principal, make, model, optional label, and createdAt timestamp. All operations are scoped to the calling principal.

Add `SavedSearch` data structure to the backend. Implement: `saveSearch(name: Text, filterJson: Text) : async Nat` (returns search ID), `getSavedSearches() : async [SavedSearch]` (returns all saved searches for calling principal), `deleteSavedSearch(id: Nat) : async Bool`, and `renameSavedSearch(id: Nat, newName: Text) : async Bool`. Each `SavedSearch` includes id, principal, name, filterJson, and createdAt. All operations are scoped to the calling principal.

Update `frontend/src/components/ExportFilterPanel.tsx` and `frontend/src/components/ComparisonExportFilterPanel.tsx` so that the saved presets sections (save, apply, rename, delete) use the per-user `useFilterPresets`, `useSaveFilterPreset`, `useDeleteFilterPreset`, and `useRenameFilterPreset` hooks — which now return only the current user's presets from the updated backend. No visual changes are required; the hooks simply now return user-scoped data automatically.

Generate a migration module (`backend/migration.mo`) that preserves all existing listings and filter presets data, while initializing the new per-principal watchlist and saved searches stable maps. The migration must not discard any previously stored listings or presets.
Allow users to set a target price for a specific make/model and flag (highlight/alert) any listings that drop below that target price

Add a `PriceAlert` data structure to the backend actor in `backend/main.mo`. Implement the following functions: `setPriceAlert(make: Text, model: Text, targetPrice: Float) : async Nat` (creates or updates a price alert for the calling principal, returns alert ID), `getPriceAlerts() : async [PriceAlert]` (returns all price alerts for the calling principal), `deletePriceAlert(id: Nat) : async Bool`. Each `PriceAlert` record includes: id (Nat), principal (Principal), make (Text), model (Text), targetPrice (Float), and createdAt (Int timestamp). All operations must be scoped to `msg.caller`. Store alerts in a stable map alongside existing data structures.

Add a backend query function `getListingsBelowTargetPrice(make: Text, model: Text) : async [Listing]` that returns all listings for the given make/model whose price is strictly less than the calling principal's stored target price for that make/model. Update `backend/migration.mo` to preserve all existing data (listings, filter presets, watchlist entries, saved searches) while initializing the new `priceAlerts` stable map as empty during canister upgrade. No existing records should be lost during migration.

Create a dedicated Saved Searches page at `frontend/src/pages/SavedSearchesPage.tsx` that displays the current user's saved searches, allows applying a search (navigating to dashboard with filters), renaming, and deleting entries. Add a navigation link in App.tsx. Gate behind Internet Identity login.

Add an in-app alert banner that appears upon login when any listings fall below the user's stored price alert targets. The banner should list affected make/model pairs with counts and link to the dashboard filtered by that make/model.
Listing deduplication — prevent duplicate entries when the same listing is imported multiple times via CSV or manual entry (e.g., deduplicate by make+model+year+mileage+price+source or listing URL)
Listing edit/update — allow users to edit existing listings in the dashboard to fix typos or update prices manually
Listing age indicator — show how old each listing is (e.g. 'Added 3 days ago') in the listings table so users know if data is stale

Add listing deduplication logic to the backend. When a listing is created (via `createListing` or `bulkCreateListings`), check for an existing listing that matches on make + model + year + mileage + price + source. If a non-empty `listingUrl` is provided, also treat a matching `listingUrl` as a duplicate. If a duplicate is detected, skip insertion and do not create a new record. `bulkCreateListings` should return the count of successfully inserted (non-duplicate) rows; duplicates are silently skipped.

Add an `updateListing(id: Nat, data: ListingData) : async Bool` function to the backend actor that allows updating all fields of an existing listing by its ID. The function should return `true` if the listing was found and updated, `false` if not found.
Onboarding empty state — when a new user has no listings, show a guided prompt to add their first listing or import a CSV
Mobile-responsive layout — ensure the dashboard table and filter panel work well on smaller screens
Pagination or infinite scroll for the dashboard listings table to handle large datasets without rendering hundreds of rows at once
Price trend indicator — show a visual trend (up/down/stable) on listings or the comparison chart to indicate whether prices for a make/model are trending up, down, or stable over recent data points
Comparison page autocomplete — add autocomplete/typeahead suggestions for make and model inputs on the ComparisonPage so users can quickly find and select car models from existing listing data

Add a backend query function `getPriceTrend(make: Text, model: Text) : async Text` that analyzes the price history for the given make/model and returns a trend label: 'up' if the average price of the most recent 30% of listings (by timestamp) is more than 5% higher than the average of the oldest 30%, 'down' if more than 5% lower, and 'stable' otherwise. The function should be callable anonymously and return 'stable' if there are fewer than 3 listings for the make/model.

Add a backend query function `getDistinctMakes() : async [Text]` that returns a deduplicated, sorted list of all make values present in the current listings store. Add a second function `getDistinctModels(make: Text) : async [Text]` that returns a deduplicated, sorted list of all model values for the given make.
